segmentation.title: Same scan. Different label.
segmentation.subtitle: Can an agent find tissue assigned to the wrong organ?
segmentation.source: BR-017 · TotalSegmentator · CC BY 4.0 · One attempt per condition

steps.title: Start with the anatomy
steps.caption: Salmon outlines the pancreas. Blue outlines the neighboring duodenum. These are views through the same 3D CT.

steps.title: Change ownership, not anatomy
steps.caption: The CT does not change. A controlled label edit assigns 21.04 mL of pancreas tissue to the duodenum.

steps.title: Follow the transferred region
steps.caption: Yellow reveals the reassigned tissue across real scan planes. This is an annotation error, not tissue moving inside the body.

steps.title: The same data, a different audit
steps.caption: Sol missed it in the broad audit. A fresh, focused audit found the correct organ and an accepted point. One run per scope.

vessels.title: Follow the vessel. Unfold the view.
vessels.subtitle: From a real segmentation gap to a linked curved CT image
vessels.source: BR-030 · ImageCAS / ImageCAS-X · Source license details in README

steps.title: A missing connection
steps.caption: A released segmentation model left an internal coronary gap. The task supplied a review region and two route endpoints.

steps.title: A local repair
steps.caption: Terra added 103 voxels and preserved the surrounding mask. Magenta marks its additions; the bright route follows the saved centerline.

steps.title: Build the curved view
steps.caption: A moving section follows the real 3D path. Linked CT samples form the flat CPR ribbon. The patient anatomy is not being stretched.

steps.title: Images right, distance labels wrong
steps.caption: Repair, tracing and mesh checks passed. The original distance axis was 8.89 mm too long. An author metadata correction fixed it; the original trial still failed.

cardiac.title: A moving shape is only part of the answer.
cardiac.subtitle: Supplied masks → Sol's mesh → independently checked tissue motion
cardiac.source: BR-035 · STRAUS simulation · Masks-only Sol condition · Original surface triangles

steps.title: Build from 30 supplied masks
steps.caption: Sol received heart-wall masks through a full simulated cycle. It built its own moving mesh; source vertex identities were withheld.

steps.title: The shape follows the cycle
steps.caption: Reference and reconstruction use the same phase and spatial scale. Mean mask overlap was 0.9461. Construction checks passed.

steps.title: Track the same material
steps.caption: The markers start at matched material positions and follow their two trajectories. They are shown through the surfaces for inspection, not selected for large errors.

steps.title: Check more than the silhouette
steps.caption: Local radial-strain error was 7.37 percentage points, above the separate 5-point research target. The example regional curve is a different, averaged measurement.

steps.title: Why shape cannot determine all motion
steps.caption: Conceptual example: a cylinder can keep the same outside shape while material twists inside it. This illustrates ambiguity, not the agent's proven error mechanism.

registration.title: Find the same point after a breath.
registration.subtitle: A local match can beat a complicated registration workflow
registration.source: BR-028 · Learn2Reg LungCT · CC BY 4.0 · One attempt per condition

steps.title: Follow an anatomical landmark
steps.caption: The source and target CTs show different breathing phases. Sol must locate the same eight points after the anatomy has moved.

steps.title: Compare the local neighborhoods
steps.caption: Source, reference and final prediction are centered independently. These review crops help inspect anatomy; their visual alignment is not a distance measurement.

steps.title: See the recovery point by point
steps.caption: With the full source CT, Sol switched from failed whole-volume methods to local matching. RMS error fell from 12.73 to 2.60 mm across fresh attempts.

steps.title: One point still breaks the rule
steps.caption: The largest error was q06 at 6.41 mm, beyond the 5 mm limit. Later visual acceptance did not change the frozen failure. The retained author baseline passed.

landmarks.title: Outside the scan, or overlooked?
landmarks.subtitle: Naming a vertebra also means knowing what the image can show
landmarks.source: BR-040 · VerSe-derived CT · CC BY-SA 4.0 · One subject, paired views

steps.title: Start with a named target
steps.caption: The task asks for named vertebral centers. A point inside real bone can still be wrong if it belongs to the wrong level.

steps.title: Remove the upper context
steps.caption: The actual cropped input ends below the T4 center. The gold line marks its boundary in the full scan; the gray area was not supplied in the cropped task.

steps.title: Abstain when the target is unavailable
steps.caption: For T4, Terra returned a point inside the crop. Sol reported out of field of view. The reference T4 center is outside the supplied volume.

steps.title: But do not miss what remains visible
steps.caption: T5 is inside the cropped scan. Sol also marked it outside, missing a visible target. Correct abstention and complete coverage must be checked separately.
